pull.title: test: split `test_IsStandard` into independent test cases
pull.body:
Part of #36692: This splits it into one test case per policy rule, each building its own transaction.

The first commit replaces `g_dust` and `g_bare_multi` globals by a `StandardPolicy` struct, which defaults to the node defaults and is passed to each check,  e.g. `CheckIsStandard(t, {.max_op_return_relay = 83})`, so no case changes policy for another. 

Second commit splits `test_IsStandard` into independent test cases i.e. one test case per policy rule. Each starts from its own standard transaction built by a new `MakeTx` helper. Since transactions are no longer carried over between checks, some values that are irrelevant to the rule under test differ from before.

Third commit builds `IsStandard` test transactions declaratively. Each check constructs its transaction in one expression instead of mutating a shared one. `CheckDustThreshold` helper also deduplicates repeated "not dust at the threshold, dust one satoshi below" from test cases.

test: build IsStandard test transactions declaratively

Construct the transaction for each check in one expression, instead of
mutating a shared transaction between checks. The input of every check
is now visible at the call site.

The repeated "not dust at the threshold, dust one satoshi below" pairs
are folded into a CheckDustThreshold helper.

No policy check is added or removed. The size of the 42-byte OP_RETURN
script, previously only implied by the hex literal, is now asserted
alongside the 83-byte one.

NIT (non-blocking): rename test from `test_IsStandard_dust` to `test_IsStandard_dust_limit` to be more clear that it is different from `test_IsStandard_dust_thresholds`

```suggestion
BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(test_IsStandard_dust_limit)
```
Good catch, they are the same script.

I think it would be nice to move this `IsStandardTx` test suite into its own file, as you are touching all lines of this test anyway. Maybe `transaction_standardness_tests.cpp`, so that it is separate from let's say tx serialize tests or other tx tests.
